display_title: Subsidieregeling Duurzame Luchtvaartbrandstoffen (SDL): e-SAF – Tijdelijke subsidieregeling Stimulering Duurzame Luchtvaartbrandstoffen (SDL)
executive_summary: The first opening round of the Dutch temporary subsidy scheme for sustainable aviation fuels (SDL), of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management and run by RVO, is open only for e-SAF (synthetic aviation fuel made from renewable hydrogen and CO2). It funds SAF project developers, companies or groups of companies with legal personality, for either a preparation project (mainly a FEED study for an investment decision, at most 60% of eligible costs, grant above EUR 4 million, finished within 24 months) or a realisation project (building, extending or converting an e-SAF production facility in the Netherlands, at most 45% of eligible costs), with 20 and 10 percentage points more for small and medium-sized companies; electrolysers for hydrogen production are not funded. The budget of EUR 205,402,000 is also the maximum per application; applications are handled first come, first served, with a lottery on the day of oversubscription, from 3 November 2026, 09:00, to 24 November 2026, 17:00.
status_rationale: The round funds FEED studies for, and the construction, extension or conversion of, commercial e-SAF production facilities in the Netherlands, excluding electrolysers for hydrogen production (Staatscourant 2026, 31133, articles 3 and 4; RVO page SDL: e-SAF, Subsidiebedragen and Voorwaarden). It touches TenneT's field only indirectly: e-SAF plants are large new electricity users, and the regulation names grid congestion and a timely grid connection as key risks for these projects, close to the project files CERRE study on flexibility and data centres and Time-dependent transmission rights contract (Lion Storage), although the call funds fuel producers rather than grid work (Toelichting hoofdstuk 6; Model projectplan SDL, Risicoanalyse). Only a SAF project developer, a company or group of companies that will develop, build and operate the SAF facility, may apply, and the rules set out no role for a grid operator, so TenneT cannot take part (article 1, SAF-projectontwikkelaar; article 3, first paragraph). The category is flexibility and demand, since the round funds new industrial power-to-liquid demand that could shape congestion and flexible load on the grid.
